name: Rosh
overview: Rosh is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as a son of Benjamin. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the family lineage that played a role in the early history of the Israelite people. His mention is brief and focused on genealogical record-keeping within the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Rosh is a proper name meaning 'head' or 'leader' in Hebrew. This name was not given by God but appears in the genealogical record in Genesis 46:21. Another name associated with the tribe of Benjamin is Rapha, meaning 'one healed,' though this name is not directly linked to Rosh.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Rosh is a son of Benjamin, establishing his direct lineage within the tribe. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text concerning Rosh.
scriptureSignificance: Rosh's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel as a son of Benjamin who migrated to Egypt. This migration is a key moment in biblical history, as it sets the stage for the Israelites' eventual sojourn and deliverance from Egypt. Although Rosh himself is not a central figure in the narrative, his inclusion affirms the continuity of the Benjaminite line during this foundational period.
